title: Michelin Star Chefs: Who Has the Most Michelin Stars?
description: The chefs with the most Michelin stars, from Yannick Alléno to Joël Robuchon’s record, what Michelin star chefs make and the youngest to win a star.
h1: Michelin Star Chefs: Who Has the Most Stars?
summary: The chefs with the most Michelin stars today and of all time, why a star belongs to the restaurant, what starred chefs earn and the youngest to win one.
keywords: who has the most michelin stars
chef with the most michelin stars
how much do michelin star chefs make
imageAlt: Illustration of five plated tasting-menu courses in a row on a cream tablecloth, each with a stack of gold stars behind it, tallest on the left.
body:
Among living chefs, Yannick Alléno has the most Michelin stars: {{names_alleno}}, across the {{names_allenoN}} restaurants that carry his name in the {{guideYear}} guides. Restaurants bearing the late Joël Robuchon’s name still hold {{names_robuchon}}, and the 32 he held in 2016 remain the record.

Strictly, though, there are no Michelin star chefs. “MICHELIN Stars are awarded to restaurants, not chefs,” as the guide itself puts it (MICHELIN Guide), so who has the most Michelin stars depends on how you count. Add up every restaurant with a chef’s name over the door and the big groups lead. Count only the kitchens a chef runs day to day and the list changes. Below are both counts, from the {{total}} starred restaurants on The Starred Bill, with the cheapest way to eat at each chef’s table.

Who has the most Michelin stars in {{guideYear}}?

These are the chefs whose names are on the most stars today: restaurants named after them, or ones they run. Where someone else leads the kitchen, that chef’s name follows the restaurant’s.

{{table:chef-names}}

Yannick Alléno: {{names_alleno}} stars

Alléno overtook Alain Ducasse in 2026 (Travel Tomorrow), when Monsieur Dior, his restaurant at 30 Montaigne in Paris, won a star seven months after opening (LVMH). He runs two three-star kitchens, Alléno Paris at the Pavillon Ledoyen and Le 1947 at Cheval Blanc in Courchevel, and the Pavillon Ledoyen alone holds six stars under one roof: three for Alléno Paris, two for L’Abysse and one for Pavyllon. He is named as head chef at {{chefTopN}} of them, which still hold {{chefTopStars}} stars between them, more than any other chef in our data. Dinner at Alléno Paris costs {{dinner:alleno-paris-au-pavillon-ledoyen}}. See our Paris page for every starred restaurant in the city.

Joël Robuchon: the record, 32 stars

Robuchon reached 32 Michelin stars in 2016, more than any chef before or since, and still held 31 when he died in August 2018 (Fine Dining Lovers). His restaurants have carried on without him: {{names_robuchonN}} of them still hold {{names_robuchon}} stars, led by the three-star Joël Robuchon in Tokyo and Robuchon au Dôme in Macau. Most are L’Atelier counters, where diners sit around an open kitchen.

Alain Ducasse: {{names_ducasse}} stars

In 2005 Ducasse became the first chef with three three-star restaurants at once, in Monaco, Paris and New York. Guinness World Records counts 21 stars won by his restaurants over his career, the most for a living chef when it checked in 2023 (Guinness World Records). Today {{names_ducasseN}} restaurants with his name hold {{names_ducasse}} stars, and he is the clearest example of a chef-owner: Emmanuel Pilon runs the kitchen at Le Louis XV in Monte Carlo and Jean-Philippe Blondet at Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester in London, both three stars. Dinner at The Dorchester costs {{dinner:alain-ducasse-at-the-dorchester}}.

Anne-Sophie Pic: {{names_pic}} stars

Pic is the most decorated woman in the guide’s history, by Guinness World Records’ count (Guinness World Records). Her family’s restaurant in Valence first won three stars in 1934, under her grandfather André, and she won them back in 2007. Restaurants with her name hold {{names_pic}} stars across {{names_picN}} kitchens, in Valence, Lausanne, Hong Kong and Bangkok. The tasting menu at Pic costs {{dinner:pic}}.

Gordon Ramsay: {{names_ramsay}} stars

Ramsay’s restaurants hold {{names_ramsay}} stars across {{names_ramsayN}} restaurants, four in London and one each in Bordeaux and Versailles. Restaurant Gordon Ramsay in Chelsea has held three since 2001, and in 2008 he held more stars than any other British chef (Fine Dining Lovers). He doesn’t cook in them day to day: Kim Ratcharoen leads the kitchen in Chelsea, where dinner costs {{dinner:restaurant-gordon-ramsay}}. Our London page lists every starred restaurant in the city, with prices.

Chef-owners and head chefs: who really holds the star?

The guide judges the food on the plate, not the name on the menu. “If a restaurant promotes a sous chef or brings in a new head chef and they maintain the same standard of cooking, then the restaurant will keep its Star,” the MICHELIN Guide explains, and inspectors eat there as often as they need to after any change in the kitchen. That is how one chef can collect more than three stars: a restaurant can hold three at most, but a chef can run, or put their name to, several.

The chef-owners at the top of the table above, Ducasse, Ramsay and Robuchon’s company after him, built groups in which trained head chefs cook to the founder’s standard, often in hotels a long way from home. Others stay at the stove. Thomas Keller is the only American chef to hold three stars at two restaurants at once, The French Laundry in California’s Napa Valley and Per Se in New York, and he still oversees both; dinner at Per Se costs {{dinner:per-se}}. When the MICHELIN Guide names a head chef, we show that chef in our restaurant lists, which is why the table below can look different from the one above.

Head chefs with the most Michelin stars

{{chefNamed}} of the world’s {{total}} starred restaurants name a head chef, and {{chefMulti}} chefs head two or more starred kitchens. Here are the {{chefListed}} with {{chefMin}} or more stars between them, counting only the restaurants each one leads. By this count the chef with the most Michelin stars is {{chefTop}}, with {{chefTopStars}} at {{chefTopN}} restaurants, ahead of {{chefSecond}}, whose 8½ Otto e Mezzo in Hong Kong is the only three-star Italian restaurant outside Italy. {{chefTwoThree}} chefs run two three-star restaurants at once: {{chefTwoThreeNames}}.

{{table:chefs}}

How much do Michelin star chefs make?

A head chef at a Michelin-starred restaurant typically earns about $80,000 to $130,000 a year in the US, £60,000 to £90,000 (about $79,000 to $119,000) in London and 10 million yen (about $63,000) or more in Tokyo, by Fine Dining Lovers’ 2026 figures. That is well above the $62,470 median for all US chefs and head cooks (US Bureau of Labor Statistics, May 2025).

The star itself pays nothing: Michelin gives no prize money. What it brings is bookings, and for a chef who owns the restaurant, a share of whatever profit is left after paying for a large brigade, costly produce and a small dining room. At the top two- and three-star restaurants, head chefs can earn £100,000 (about $132,000) or more in London, and more than $150,000 in New York once bonuses and profit-sharing are counted. Further down the kitchen, sous chefs earn about £40,000 to £55,000 ($53,000 to $73,000) in London and $70,000 to $85,000 in New York. The chef-owners at the top of this page earn most of their money away from the stove, from television, books and the hotels and groups that put their names over the door.

Who is the youngest Michelin star chef?

Michelin keeps no official record, but the youngest chefs to win stars were 22. Gilles Epié is usually named as the youngest ever to win one, at Le Pavillon des Princes in Paris, where he had been given the kitchen at 21 (France-Amérique). The MICHELIN Guide calls E.J. Lagasse the youngest chef ever to lead a two-star restaurant: he was 22 when Emeril’s in New Orleans, his father Emeril’s restaurant, won two stars in November 2025 (MICHELIN Guide). Dinner there costs {{dinner:emerils}}.

Massimiliano Alajmo was the same age when Le Calandre, his family’s restaurant near Padua, won its second star in 1996, and he holds the three-star record: Le Calandre won its third in 2002, when he was 28, the youngest three-star chef in the guide’s history (Fine Dining Lovers). He still leads the kitchen, where the tasting menu costs {{dinner:le-calandre}}. Before him the record was Marco Pierre White’s, at 33 in 1995. White handed all his stars back in 1999, saying he had achieved everything he set out to (Wikipedia).

Michelin star chef records

  • Most stars ever: Joël Robuchon, 32 in 2016.
  • Most stars today: {{nameLiving}}, {{nameLivingStars}} across {{nameLivingN}} restaurants.
  • Most stars won over a career by a living chef: Alain Ducasse, 21, by Guinness World Records’ count in 2023.
  • First chef with three three-star restaurants at once: Alain Ducasse, in 2005.
  • Most-starred woman: Anne-Sophie Pic, whose restaurants hold {{names_pic}} today.

More about Michelin star chefs

For the chefs behind every starred Indian restaurant, from Himanshu Saini’s three stars in Dubai to Garima Arora in Bangkok, see Indian chefs with Michelin stars. How inspectors decide, and what happens to a star when the chef leaves, is in How do restaurants get a Michelin star?, and the world’s top tables, with their chefs and prices, are in every three-Michelin-star restaurant. faq.q: Who has the most Michelin stars?
faq.a: Among living chefs, {{nameLiving}}, whose {{nameLivingN}} restaurants hold {{nameLivingStars}} stars in the {{guideYear}} guides. Restaurants carrying the late Joël Robuchon’s name still hold {{names_robuchon}}, and his 32 in 2016 are the most any chef has ever held.

faq.q: Do chefs or restaurants get Michelin stars?
faq.a: Restaurants. The MICHELIN Guide awards its stars to restaurants, not chefs, and a restaurant keeps its stars under a new head chef if the cooking stays as good. Chefs who run several starred restaurants are often said to hold all their stars.

faq.q: Can a chef have more than three Michelin stars?
faq.a: Yes, across several restaurants. One restaurant can hold three stars at most, but a chef who runs or owns more than one can add them up: {{chefTop}} leads {{chefTopN}} starred kitchens with {{chefTopStars}} stars between them.

faq.q: How many Michelin stars does Gordon Ramsay have?
faq.a: {{names_ramsay}}, across {{names_ramsayN}} restaurants in the {{guideYear}} guides. Three are at Restaurant Gordon Ramsay in Chelsea, which has kept them since 2001; head chefs run each of his kitchens day to day.

faq.q: Which female chef has the most Michelin stars?
faq.a: Anne-Sophie Pic. Restaurants carrying her name hold {{names_pic}} stars across {{names_picN}} kitchens, led by three-star Pic in Valence, France, and Guinness World Records names her the most decorated woman in the guide’s history.

faq.q: Which American chef has the most Michelin stars?
faq.a: Thomas Keller, with {{names_keller}} stars: three each at The French Laundry in Napa Valley and Per Se in New York, and one at The Surf Club Restaurant in Miami. He is the only American chef to hold three stars at two restaurants at once.
